neighbours.label: reporting a statistical test's finding: the words right after 'showed/indicated/revealed' (showed a significant effect, a statistical significance for)
fire: A two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction between dose and time.
The t-test indicated a significant difference between the two classes.
The chi-square analysis revealed a statistical significance for female patients.
Logistic regression showed a significant association between smoking and stroke.
The Kruskal-Wallis test showed a significant effect of diet on weight gain.
The correlation analysis indicated a strong relationship between sleep and mood.
Analysis of covariance showed a significant main effect of training.
The mosaic plot indicates a statistically significant link for the older group.
quiet: A two-way design was used to study the dose and timing of the treatment.
The class took a test on fractions just before the holidays.
The chi-square table is printed at the back of the textbook.
Patients who smoke were asked about their diet and exercise.
Mice on the new diet were weighed every morning for a month.
Participants kept a diary of their sleep and mood for two weeks.
The training lasted six weeks and took place in the evenings.
The mosaic plot uses coloured boxes to show the size of each group.

notes: Probe: 'ANOVA showed a significant effect' 0.49, 'indicates a statistical significance for' 0.33, 'regression revealed a strong association between' 0.26; plotting code 0.01-0.02 (plt branch from card not reproduced), 'clear difference between the two groups' 0.13.
